target.title: improve: native iOS look with stock SwiftUI navigation, forms, chat, and talk visualizer
target.body:
Closes #99195

> 🤖 AI-assisted (built with Claude Code; every screen iterated and verified on the iOS Simulator with maintained-human review of each step).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iPhone users navigating the iOS app would see non-native, custom-built UI chrome (floating shadowed cards, hand-rolled headers with hidden navigation bars, custom capsule switches, `.roundedBorder` inputs, status pills, gradient avatars) on every tab, making the app feel un-Apple-like and inconsistent with iOS platform conventions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaces the custom "Pro" component chrome with stock SwiftUI throughout the phone app: real navigation bars (large titles, native back/push, `.searchable`, toolbar menus), `List`/`Form` inset-grouped sections with `LabeledContent`/`Toggle`/`Picker` rows, iMessage-style chat (visible receiver bubbles + iOS 26 glass composer with mic→send swapping, availability-gated), native `ContentUnavailableView` empty/error states, and a new Siri-style Talk waveform (Canvas + TimelineView, MIT-attributed math) that renders the runtime's real states: off = static grey, connecting/thinking = slow breathing, listening = mic-level reactive, speech = full, agent speaking = pulsing. Copy is trimmed to single-line rows per Apple convention. Rebuilt on top of the recent design refresh on `main`; the already-nativized Agents surfaces from `main` are kept as-is. Non-goals: iPad sidebar layouts and Settings sub-flows beyond the converted forms.

## User Impact

The app now looks and behaves like a native iOS app: standard navigation transitions and back buttons everywhere, familiar Settings-style forms, an iMessage-like chat, pull-to-refresh + native search on Agents, and a Talk screen that visibly reacts to your voice and clearly shows when the mic is off. Net −84 LOC in this diff (removes more custom UI than it adds).

## Evidence

- Built and ran every screen on iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.2), Debug, via XcodeBuildMCP; all five tabs launch clean on this branch after rebasing onto current `main` (chat/talk/control/agent/settings smoke: ALIVE).
- Verified per-screen with simulator screenshots at each iteration, including width-alignment audit across tabs and a pixel comparison of the Settings large-title metrics against Apple's stock Settings app on the same simulator (identical).
- Talk waveform states verified live (static grey when off; reacts to power/state changes).
- Before/after screenshots for all core screens attached in the first comment below.
